summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the feelings program arrives as a physical object in everybody's way. Middle image: Astra and the local cards establish the actual boundary. Closing image: Zib immediately converts the abstract program into a workplace problem.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Morning in the bullpen; the Bring Your Feelings to Work Day table sits awkwardly in the normal traffic path under the cheerful required-participation / optional-disclosure placard.
PANEL 2 — Astra gives the plain local rule while coworkers continue arriving and working around the table.
PANEL 3 — Glorp checks the valid ENTRY / NO ENTRY states against the local cards Kreeb has placed beside the corporate tablet.
PANEL 4 — Zib stands with a cart blocked by the table and makes the first practical complaint of the day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Bring Your Feelings to Work Day. A small box, one afternoon, and apparently a shipping crate of stationery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Someone might actually want to tell us something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: People tell us things already. Then someone puts them on a form and they stop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Can one of them tell you the west corridor's been whining for three days?

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing directly from the opening table scene. Opening image: Jax tests the no-entry boundary first. Middle image: Pixa changes its own behavior before anyone requests it. Closing image: Noola recognizes the learning while the program keeps moving.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax marks NO ENTRY and hands the card across the table while ordinary traffic continues behind him.
PANEL 2 — Pixa completes the participation state but pauses before sending any public confirmation.
PANEL 3 — Pixa asks whether Jax wants private confirmation, surprising Jax and Glorp.
PANEL 4 — Noola notices the change in Pixa's behavior as the confirmation goes only to Jax's handheld.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Do I have to write a feeling to get into the corridor?

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: No. The box is voluntary. I can also decline to record your silence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: I'm only keeping the maintenance reports. Nobody's personal life belongs in the same folder.

dialogueInline.speaker: Noola Vaneel
dialogueInline.text: That's encouraging. I was about to submit a complaint about the box itself.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the same morning. Opening image: the first disclosure refuses the program's expected shape. Middle image: Zib and Kreeb respond to what the worker actually wrote. Closing image: the card physically leaves the feelings table and becomes work.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The first free-text card appears at the table: VENT BY BERTH 3 WHISTLES ALL NIGHT.
PANEL 2 — Glorp objects to its category while Zib reads the actual sentence and immediately recognizes a job.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb reframes the submission as useful information rather than a failed feeling entry while Zib starts gathering tools.
PANEL 4 — Astra authorizes maintenance routing on the spot and Zib leaves with the physical card.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Here. My feeling is that the corridor makes a horrible noise every fourth cycle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: That's a service complaint. We can actually do something with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: It also sounds extremely personal when you say it that way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: The machine is whining. I'm being polite.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Have someone check the actual machine before anybody starts interpreting the card.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Berth 3 service corridor. Opening image: the complaint is immediately audible in the real location. Middle image: the repair team follows the sound instead of the program categories. Closing image: a feeling-day card becomes a normal maintenance diagnosis.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — At Berth 3, Jax arrives with a ladder and hears the whistle before Zib points anything out.
PANEL 2 — Zib puts Jax on the ladder while the sound continues from the grille.
PANEL 3 — They remove the cover and find the loose edge visibly vibrating against the frame.
PANEL 4 — Zib marks the ordinary defect on the original disclosure card while Jax mourns the loss of a more dramatic explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: There it is again. From behind Berth Three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I heard it Tuesday. Thought it was the cleaning cart.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: And you didn't mention it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I told the cart driver he had a terrible cart.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Good. We've narrowed it down to every moving part in the corridor.

settingText: Berth 3 service corridor on Stardust Station; sleeping-berth wall, accessible ventilation grille, ordinary hand tools and a narrow maintained service chase.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the program produces three kinds of information at once. Middle image: Pixa and Mira preserve the distinctions instead of collapsing them. Closing image: the personal card remains visibly unconverted.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in operations, three very different cards sit apart on the table: cold-sticking hatch, conflicting handoff checklists, and I MISS HOME ON LATE SHIFT.
PANEL 2 — Pixa identifies that the three entries request different outcomes without deriving a common emotion category.
PANEL 3 — Mira reacts with genuine pleasure at the clean separation while Pixa absorbs the feedback.
PANEL 4 — Astra routes the hatch to field work and Glorp takes the checklist problem to the people who actually use it.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb keeps the personal card out of both work streams; Noola sees the distinction from across the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Some cards describe feelings, some describe equipment, and one appears to be a restaurant review.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I can test the noise. I can't test whether the cafe deserved one star.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Do we know who left the card?

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: We shouldn't. That's why the box is anonymous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: I think I recognize the handwriting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Noola Vaneel
dialogueInline.text: That's exactly what an anonymous box needs. Amateur detectives.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: I'll leave the author field empty. The words are enough for the repair.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in East hatch service area. Opening image: the complaint appears false under the wrong test condition. Middle image: Jax and Mira reproduce the actual environment. Closing image: the physical defect reveals itself exactly as the worker described.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — At the east hatch, Jax cycles the door at room temperature and it works perfectly.
PANEL 2 — Mira rereads the complaint and points out the condition Jax has not reproduced yet.
PANEL 3 — Jax inspects the lower guide while Mira opens the thermal history and prepares the cold test.
PANEL 4 — The guide is cooled to late-shift conditions and the hatch begins to bind.
PANEL 5 — Jax finds the contact point before Mira finishes opening the graph, giving them a shared victory rather than a lecture.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: It won't make the noise with the hatch open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Then close it and run the same cycle as the complaint. I want to hear what they heard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I like this part of science. The part where we admit the first test didn't prove anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: You mostly like being allowed to do something twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: If the second time counts as work, yes.

settingText: East hatch service area in Stardust Station's maintained corridor network; ordinary access hardware, thermal history display, guide track and safe local test area.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the complaint is investigated through the actual work documents. Middle image: the process, not a worker, emerges as the defect. Closing image: Glorp prioritizes repair over classification.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp and Kreeb spread the two current night-shift handoff checklists beside fresh notes from their users.
PANEL 2 — They establish that both versions are current and both are genuinely in use.
PANEL 3 — The overlap becomes visible: each list assumes a task the other schedules at a different point.
PANEL 4 — Glorp circles the process conflict while Astra asks how to classify the original disclosure.
PANEL 5 — Glorp moves the category field aside and starts drafting one reconciled checklist; Kreeb and Astra enjoy the novelty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: The card says 'during the late cycle.' The maintenance log says we never tested it late.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Then someone was describing a real problem. We made it sound like a mood.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Can we send the specific timing to Zib?

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Already did. I didn't include who might've written the card.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Good. It's embarrassing enough when your own coworkers think they can recognize you from a complaint.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the anonymous box produces the day's least actionable disclosure. Middle image: Brick claims the case while Astra refuses automatic escalation. Closing image: the joke runs in the foreground as Kreeb protects the personal card in the background.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Brick retrieves THE VENDING MACHINE IS SMUG from the anonymous drop box and studies it with inappropriate seriousness.
PANEL 2 — Jax recognizes the note as Brick's natural jurisdiction and encourages him.
PANEL 3 — Brick turns toward the vending machine while Astra sets the threshold for what may actually become work.
PANEL 4 — As Brick continues objecting, Kreeb quietly takes the I MISS HOME card out of the public pile and leaves for the quiet room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: This card is unmistakably the work of someone with a grievance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: It's an anonymous box. That describes literally everybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: I don't think that's fair to everybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: The phrase 'a persistent whine' narrows my suspects.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Don't look at me like that. I only make noise when I'm right.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Put the case away, Brick. Zib has an actual wrench and an actual problem.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Quiet Room. Opening image: Noola claims the card privately. Middle image: she states the feeling without converting it into a defect. Closing image: Kreeb accepts that expression itself can be the entire outcome.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the quiet room, Kreeb places the personal card in the locked local envelope as Noola enters and identifies it as hers.
PANEL 2 — Noola explains that late shift makes her miss home and that she wanted somewhere to say it, not a repair ticket.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb asks only whether she wants anything changed, accepts no for an answer, and lets the conversation end without solving her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Noola Vaneel
dialogueInline.text: I wrote the one about people asking if I'm all right.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Oh. I thought you were annoyed about the quiet room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Noola Vaneel
dialogueInline.text: I like the room. I don't like being told what my water rig must feel like by people who have never worn it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Have I done that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Noola Vaneel
dialogueInline.text: Quite often. But I like you, so I've been kind about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: I was going to ask how you are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Noola Vaneel
dialogueInline.text: You may ask whether the room is warm. Then I'll tell you.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in East hatch service area. Opening image: diagnosis returns as verification work. Middle image: the team recreates the exact complaint condition after repair. Closing image: the worker's disclosure becomes a closed, tested maintenance result.
settingText: East hatch service area in Stardust Station's maintained corridor network; ordinary access hardware, thermal history display, guide track and safe local test area.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax, Mira and Zib return to the east hatch with a thin shim and the cold-test setup.
PANEL 2 — Zib insists on reproducing the failure after the repair rather than trusting a single good cycle.
PANEL 3 — Jax installs the shim while Mira resets the cold condition.
PANEL 4 — The hatch cycles cleanly at the problem temperature and all three watch the same physical proof.
PANEL 5 — Jax closes the ticket with VERIFIED COLD while Zib undercuts his attempt at dramatic commentary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: It makes the same noise when the return cycle starts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: And not when the hatch is open. We've reproduced the condition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: The coupling vibrates just enough to hit the cover.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I owe the cart driver an apology.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Buy him a replacement wheel and we'll call it even.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Berth 3 service corridor. Opening image: the final adjustment is small and physical. Middle image: the repair is tested by listening. Closing image: only ordinary airflow remains, and the original disclosure card closes as maintenance.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back at Berth 3, Zib reseats the vent grille while Jax restores airflow.
PANEL 2 — Both stop and listen in the corridor after power returns.
PANEL 3 — Only ordinary air remains; Zib closes the original disclosure card as maintenance while Jax enjoys the silence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: I'll adjust the coupling. Keep your ear by the cover, not your head inside it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Silence. I haven't heard that much silence since Kreeb tried the quiet room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Then it's fixed. Tell Glorp the card was useful. Don't tell Brick it was evidence.

settingText: Berth 3 service corridor on Stardust Station; sleeping-berth wall, accessible ventilation grille, ordinary hand tools and a narrow maintained service chase.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the useful outcomes now live on an ordinary work board. Middle image: process and equipment fixes return to normal station life. Closing image: Noola's unresolved feeling coexists with a productive day without being turned into a metric.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — By afternoon, the work board shows several concrete repairs and one reconciled process originating from the morning disclosures.
PANEL 2 — Glorp posts the single handoff checklist while removing the conflicting pair.
PANEL 3 — Pixa carries the repaired stool back to its normal place and reports the operational closure counts while Astra and Glorp notice the unassigned helpfulness.
PANEL 4 — Noola passes Kreeb near the nearly irrelevant participation table; her personal issue remains private and unchanged.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: The noise complaint is closed. The repair record doesn't include anybody's private card.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: That seems fair. They told us enough to find it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Noola Vaneel
dialogueInline.text: And someone else now gets to walk that corridor without the noise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That is worth more than knowing who wrote it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: I've kept the equipment trace. It describes the change perfectly well.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the institutional system finally reacts to the day's low category completion. Middle image: the request conflicts with the distinctions the crew preserved. Closing image: Astra sets a factual reporting boundary.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The corporate dashboard finally objects: LOW CATEGORY COMPLETION MAY LIMIT INTERPRETABILITY.
PANEL 2 — A second request asks for de-identified disclosure themes and output correlation, trying to pull the different outcomes back into one model.
PANEL 3 — Mira rejects the unsupported correlation while Kreeb closes the local personal envelope.
PANEL 4 — Glorp points to routed work and completion states; Pixa adds that no inferred categories were created.
PANEL 5 — Astra orders the response to use only the information the day actually produced.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Central says participation is low and the disclosure categories are incomplete.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: The crew came to work. They repaired a real fault. That should count as something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: The lab numbers don't support a relationship between a statement and residue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: They want us to sort private stories into named categories anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: People told us things because they trusted us, not because they wanted a scoring system.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: the material numbers do not match the day's operational success in an obvious way. Middle image: Mira is curious before she is cautious. Closing image: the unresolved comparison stays open as a question rather than becoming a claim.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the lab, Mira lines up the lower passive sample total beside the unusually productive workday.
PANEL 2 — The mismatch catches Mira's attention before Astra asks what kind of 'huh' she is making.
PANEL 3 — Astra offers the tempting causal explanation that fixing things lowered output; Mira keeps the possibility open without accepting it.
PANEL 4 — Mira records MATERIAL EFFECT: INDETERMINATE and leaves the comparison visible for future curiosity.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: We have two residue readings, and one of them is too small to interpret.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Yet the repair worked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: The maintenance record is more complete than the material record.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Of course. Zib didn't have to discover a new physical phenomenon to tighten a coupling.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: aggregate reporting creates one last privacy trap. Middle image: Glorp recognizes and removes it. Closing image: Brick's joke case remains deliberately outside the formal report.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp builds the aggregate report while Kreeb checks whether even the no-entry count is safe on a six-person shift.
PANEL 2 — The privacy problem becomes obvious once the small population is stated aloud.
PANEL 3 — Glorp removes the count himself before Astra can finish asking, preserving only the rule that no-entry was accepted.
PANEL 4 — Brick presents the vending-machine note as the last unresolved case and Glorp rejects it from the report.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: The anonymous submissions contain several striking omissions.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: An omission in an anonymous submission is usually called privacy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: If people want to tell us more, they'll tell us themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: That's a surprisingly unsatisfying investigative technique.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: It's also the one we're keeping.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing directly from the aggregate-report work. Opening image: the final response is built from completed operational outcomes. Middle image: each specialist contributes one bounded piece. Closing image: the report leaves with fewer categories and more clarity.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra writes the final report beside the completed work board rather than the participation table.
PANEL 2 — Mira adds the unresolved material question as a bounded physical result.
PANEL 3 — Glorp and Kreeb add the privacy boundary they built together: no personal count and no personal text.
PANEL 4 — Pixa compares the short outgoing report with the much larger source form and finds the reduction useful rather than alarming.
PANEL 5 — Astra submits the readable report without adding any reconstructed categories.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: We'll report the noise repair and the physical observations. Nothing personal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Say we don't know whether the material readings have anything to do with the cards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Done. And the author fields stay empty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: You can say the quiet room worked for people who chose it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: I've recorded it as an available space. No attendance roster.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the reporting scene. Opening image: remote interpretation fails. Middle image: the company responds by sending a human observer. Closing image: the next issue's pressure enters as a person, not another form.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The corporate reply appears immediately: REMOTE INTERPRETATION INCONCLUSIVE.
PANEL 2 — ON-SITE OPERATIONS LIAISON RECOMMENDED follows beneath it; Jax realizes the next interpretive tool is an actual person.
PANEL 3 — Astra opens the visitor-preparation attachment while Jax points out that forms do not normally walk around looking at things.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Central hasn't accepted the difference between low disclosure and no useful work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: They should visit. They'll hear a station without that terrible whine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: They're sending a liaison. An actual person.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Oh. That's more alarming than the box.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing directly from the liaison notice. Opening image: the crew moves from report to preparation without a scene reset. Middle image: Jax takes ownership before being asked. Closing image: Pixa formalizes the responsibility he tried to play down.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra opens the visitor-prep list and tells the room not to panic while Jax is already reaching for the route sheet.
PANEL 2 — Astra catches Jax volunteering before she assigns anything.
PANEL 3 — Jax claims the visitor route as his existing responsibility and immediately regrets sounding proud of it.
PANEL 4 — Pixa records Jax as route owner while Jax protests the public confirmation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: We have a visitor next week. I want the route clear and the evidence ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I'll check the route. Please don't make me memorize a speech about how lovely the corridors are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Would you like the tour to include the place we just repaired?

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Yes. We actually did something there.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the visitor-prep scene. Opening image: the default checklist tries to turn the station into a presentation. Middle image: Astra deletes performance rather than clutter. Closing image: only operational readiness remains.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The default visitor checklist opens with PRESENTATION / SIGNAGE / VISIBLE CLUTTER / STAFF READINESS.
PANEL 2 — Astra rejects most of the performative list while Zib asks which part she means.
PANEL 3 — Astra looks around the visibly working station and refuses to stage it as if nobody works there.
PANEL 4 — The surviving list contains only safety hazards, access and required records; Zib finally approves of a visitor plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: You've made a presentation of the service corridor. It has a wall, some pipes, and two doors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: It's also where we fixed a real problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Then let them see it. Don't put a velvet rope around the manifold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't going to put a velvet rope anywhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Good. I hate moving velvet ropes.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the visitor-prep sequence. Opening image: private material is kept local. Middle image: the bounded science result joins the packet. Closing image: Brick's comic obsession tests the boundary and loses.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp and Kreeb keep the personal envelope physically outside the visitor packet while the prep work continues at the same table.
PANEL 2 — Mira adds only the bounded material note: no behavioral predictor identified.
PANEL 3 — Brick approaches with his folded vending-machine note as if it belongs in the unresolved-items stack.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb recognizes the note before Brick can explain it and blocks the escalation.
PANEL 5 — Brick states the accusation anyway; Glorp keeps it out of the visitor packet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: I've gathered the records that show what we know and what we don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Please leave in the failed tests. Those are the ones I can explain honestly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: And no one is giving the liaison copies of anonymous cards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: Should I brief our visitor on the unresolved case of the bright chair?

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: You may brief the chair. The visitor has enough to do.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the same preparation scene. Opening image: the visitor becomes real. Middle image: Jax's pride turns into practical route checking. Closing image: the route is actually ready.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — VISITOR CONFIRMED: STARTRUST OPERATIONS LIAISON appears while Jax is already walking his route.
PANEL 2 — Jax checks the same intersection again because the nearby collection bin tends to drift when bumped.
PANEL 3 — Pixa calls out the repeated check without mocking him, and Jax makes the final clearance adjustment.
PANEL 4 — Astra asks whether the route is ready; Jax finally gives a direct yes instead of a territorial answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: The visitor's arrival time is confirmed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I'll check the route from the dock. Last time a guest got lost behind the spare-chair cupboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That guest was a delivery driver.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Yes. He stayed for lunch and recommended the vending-machine curry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: I still haven't met anyone who agrees with him.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Brick finally receives the evidence he thinks he wanted. Middle image: Pixa refuses the inference in the same language the crew has used all day. Closing image: the vending-machine joke carries directly into the approaching liaison visit.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Late cycle, Brick selects water at the vending machine and receives a protein bar under SELECTION OPTIMIZED.
PANEL 2 — Pixa passes as Brick presents the substitution as evidence; Pixa refuses to infer intent.
PANEL 3 — Brick repeats the accusation while Pixa announces the visitor's arrival in eleven hours; Brick tells the incoming liaison to bring exact change.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: I have identified the author of the anonymous note.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: No. You've identified three people who use the word 'whine.'

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: That's an unusually broad suspect pool.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: The sound is fixed, Brick. The case can go home.
